data.name: Bairavi
data.gender_notes: Bairavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess Bairavi is a form of Goddess Lakshmi, who is known to bring happiness, prosperity, and contentment. She is the embodiment of compassion, grace, and strength. The name Bairavi carries the meaning “Bringer of happiness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bairavi usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bairavi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bringer of happiness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bairavi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

celebrity_usage: Bairavi is a popular name among Tamil speaking communities in India.
data.cultural_impact: Goddess Bairavi is revered in Tamil Nadu, South India, and holds great significance in the Hindu culture. Her festivals and celebrations are an essential part of the Tamil calendar. In Hindu mythology, she is considered the goddess of speech, eloquence, and learning. She is believed to bless her devotees with ability to express themselves effectively and convey their thoughts articulately.
data.spiritual_significance: Goddess Bairavi represents the feminine aspect of divinity - associated with nurturing, compassion, grace, and strength. Her name signifies the removal of fears and worries, instilling peace and tranquility in the hearts of the devotees. She is also believed to bestow upon her followers the power of speech and good communication skills. Worshipping Goddess Bairavi is said to bring happiness, prosperity, and contentment in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bairavi is the embodiment of compassion and consolation. Her name signifies the soothing effect of her presence, calming turbulent emotions and offering solace in times of distress.

historical_references.reference: Bairavi is an aspect of the Hindu deity Shiva's consort Parvati, also known as Bhavani or Bhairavi. She is depicted as the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and the arts, particularly music and dance.
historical_references.context: Medieval Hinduism, Shiva and Shakti worship

historical_references.reference: The name Bairavi is also associated with a group of female deities known as the Yogini or Shaktini, who were revered in ancient India for their protective and healing powers. These deities were believed to be the embodiment of various aspects of Shakti, the divine feminine energy, and Bairavi was one of their prominent names.
historical_references.context: Ancient Hinduism, Goddess worship and Tantra

modern_usage.modern_context: Bairavi is a popular Hindu goddess revered for her soothing and calming nature. In the modern context, her name is associated with various trends. In the realm of music, Bairavi is often used as the title of devotional compositions, particularly in Carnatic music. Her name is also used to label soothing and calming music playlists on streaming platforms such as Spotify and Apple Music. In the field of yoga and meditation, Bairavi is invoked as a deity to promote peace and tranquility during practices. Additionally, her name is also referenced in various art and cultural contexts, such as in traditional paintings and sculptures depicting her. The Hindu goddess Bairavi is thus a symbol of peace, tranquility, and calmness in the modern world, and her name is seen on various platforms in these diverse contexts.
